title: Scheduled plan downgrades and pro-rata refund rules — requirements and billing acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures product requirements, scope decisions, and acceptance criteria for supporting scheduled plan downgrades with automated pro-rata refunds and credits. The feature enables customers to schedule a downgrade (e.g., from Premium to Standard) to take effect at a future billing boundary or immediate date, and receive accurate, auditable credit/refund calculations and invoices. It must integrate with per-route quotas, burst credits, and emergency burst windows without causing invoice inconsistency or double-credits.

Background and motivation:
Customers frequently request the ability to schedule account changes to align with internal budget cycles or contract end-dates. Current manual adjustments require support intervention and produce delayed, error-prone refunds. Automating scheduled downgrades reduces ops overhead, improves self-serve experience, and reduces refund disputes.

Key product goals:
- Provide a deterministic pro-rata calculation engine that accounts for: plan entitlements (quota sizes and concurrency), per-route reserved capacity, consumed ephemeral credits (burst), and overage charges during the billing period.
- Ensure invoices and balance adjustments are explainable and match the console billing preview.
- Guarantee no customer-visible regressions (no negative balances, double credits, or missed refunds) during rollout.
- Surface a clear audit trail and refund reason codes for finance reconciliation.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- Finance: Maria Gonzalez (billing reconciliation)
- Eng: Liam Chen (assignee), ENG Billing & Metering team
- Legal/Compliance: compliance-review required for regulated accounts
- Support: onboarding doc and playbook required

Interaction with existing features:
- Must honor soft-burst windows and credit anchoring: if a customer consumed burst credits earlier in the billing cycle, pro-rate should invoice consumed credits and only refund unused committed credits.
- Rate limits and token quotas are unchanged until the downgrade effective time. Post-effective time enforcement must reflect the downgraded entitlements.
- Scheduled downgrades that collide with a scheduled model/region migration should apply the later of the two effective times and surface a warning to the user.

Scope (in):
- UI/Console: scheduling flow with effective date selector, preview of pro-rata delta, and confirmation modal with refund breakdown.
- API: new endpoint POST /v1/plan_changes with body {effective_at, target_plan, apply_credits: boolean} and GET /v1/plan_changes/{id}/preview returning a line-itemized pro-rata object.
- Billing engine: adjustable proration pipeline that computes credits/refunds and emits invoice adjustments with reason codes.
- Audit logs: record who scheduled, when, the preview shown, and the final settled amount.
- Acceptance tests and reconciliation reports for finance.

Scope (out):
- Manual refunds initiated by Support outside the automated schedule (handled by separate support tooling ticket).
- Complex cross-account credit transfers (future work).

Open product decisions needing design/finance sign-off:
1) Proration basis: bill-time vs. usage-time. Recommendation: usage-time for token-based consumption (refund based on actual consumed units) and bill-time for flat-seat components. Requires finance approval.
2) Treatment of overages consumed prior to the effective time: should be charged on final invoice and excluded from refund calculations. (Proposed: charge first, refund only unused committed quota.)
3) Scheduled downgrade conflicts: whether to auto-reschedule or require manual resolution. (Proposed: warn and surface a single-confirm step that will confirm the later effective date.)

Migration and rollback plan:
- Phase 1 (shadow mode): implement proration engine in shadow and produce preview reports for a subset of customers (opt-in). No invoices altered.
- Phase 2 (limited rollout): enable on non-enterprise customers with low financial risk. Finance to reconcile sample invoices daily.
- Phase 3 (full rollout): enable feature by default and deprecate manual-support refunds for scheduled downgrades.
- Rollback: if reconciliation mismatch > 0.5% for 48h, revert to Phase 1 and freeze scheduled changes (notify customers).

Acceptance criteria (billing and product):
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Preview parity — For a set of 200 historical billing samples, the API preview output must match the final settled invoice within $0.10 for 99.5% of samples when run in shadow mode.

AC-2: No double-credits — When a scheduled downgrade executes, the billing engine must not issue a credit that duplicates an earlier burst credit; verified via reconciliation logs and automated assertions.

AC-3: Auditability — Every scheduled change must generate an immutable audit entry containing (scheduler, scheduled_at, effective_at, target_plan, preview_hash, settled_invoice_id) visible in Console and downloadable as CSV.

AC-4: Rate-limit continuity — Requests during the grace window (between scheduling and effective_at) must be served using pre-change entitlements; post-effective checks must reflect downgraded entitlements within 5 seconds of enforcement flip.

AC-5: Financial settlement timing — Refunds or account credits generated by pro-rata calculations must land in the customer billing ledger within the next invoice cycle and be tagged with a reason code 'SCHEDULED_DOWNGRADE' for accounting reconciliation.
AC-6: Edge-case: mid-period plan upgrade followed by scheduled downgrade — system must compute a net delta based on the time-weighted entitlements (tests included).
AC-7: Supportability — Support playbook created and validated with two support agents performing end-to-end scheduled downgrades in sandbox without manual Finance intervention.
AC-8: Monitoring & Alerts — Reconciliation error rate > 0.5% triggers a P1 pager to Finance and Billing Eng, with an automated snapshot of 24h impacted invoices.
AC-9: Compliance — For accounts flagged as regulated, scheduled downgrades must require an additional approval step (UI checkbox + two-person confirmation) and produce an exportable audit bundle.
AC-10: API contract stability — The new endpoints must be backward compatible: GET previews return only additional optional fields and existing client calls without preview fields continue to work.
AC-11: Idempotency — Re-submitting the same plan change request (same scheduler idempotency token) before execution must not create duplicate change records or credits.
test_plan: Unit tests for proration math, integration tests that run end-to-end on staging with synthetic usage traces (including burst consumption, overages, and credits), and finance reconciliation job that compares shadow preview vs final invoice. QA to validate Console preview, API preview, and invoice adjustments. Load test: schedule 10k downgrades/day to validate pipeline throughput.
monitoring: Dashboards: scheduled-change-success-rate, preview-vs-final-delta, reconciliation-error-rate, execution-latency (time from effective_at to enforcement). Alerts: reconciliation-error-rate > 0.5% (P1), preview-vs-final-delta median > $0.50 (P2).
implementation_notes: Engineering must extend the metering pipeline to expose time-weighted entitlements and tag consumed units with plan-version metadata. Billing team to provide mapping from plan SKUs to accounting GL codes. Ensure preview endpoint signs a content-hash for non-repudiation. UX to show top 3 line items causing the delta (committed quota, burst credits, overage).
rollout_notes: Start with a 2-week shadow run for 250 opt-in customers. Finance to validate daily samples. After sign-off, enable gradual traffic on a feature flag with 5%, 25%, 100% ramps. Communicate change via release notes and customer emails.
notes: Design and Finance to finalize proration basis decision by 2025-11-18. ENG to provide prototype preview API by 2025-11-29. Coordinate with Compliance for regulated account gating.
